The round follows 300% year-over-year revenue growth and more than doubled OLIGO's valuation since its Series B, which we were proud to lead. It comes on the back of a strong year: OLIGO became AWS's exclusive AI runtime security partner for Security Hub Extended, joined Palantir's FedStart Program on the path to FedRAMP High and DoD IL5, and launched Runtime Exploit Blocking at the application layer.
Runtime is where the business lives, and OLIGO solved the hardest problem in security: protecting production without trading security for uptime. Doubling down was an easy call. Glad to be building alongside Canon Capital, Greenfield Partners, Lightspeed, Red Dot Capital Partners, and TLV Partners. [...] Excited to share that our portfolio company OLIGO Security has raised $60M in additional funding, bringing their total funding to $140M. Proud to be backing them again since leading their Series B.
What stands out to me is not just the round, their ARR grew 300% year over year. That is a go-to-market engine finding its gear.
GTM in cybersecurity lives on proving what is real. Oligo sells into teams buried in alerts, and the pitch only lands when the product can show what is genuinely exploitable. Runtime makes that conversation concrete.

results.title: Oligo Security raises $60M as AI speeds up exploit development - SiliconANGLE
results.content:
UPDATED 11:00 EDT / AUGUST 04 2026

### Oligo Security raises $60M as AI speeds up exploit development

by  Duncan Riley

Runtime security startup Oligo Security Ltd. said today that it had raised $60 million in new funding to accelerate product innovation and expand global go-to-market operations.

Oligo’s software sits alongside applications in production. A sensor built on eBPF, the Linux kernel feature, tracks which library functions a workload actually calls. Most of the vulnerabilities a scanner flags are never called at all, and those are the ones Oligo tells customers they can leave alone. The ones that do get called can be blocked mid-exploit at the application layer, without killing the container or the process behind it. [...] Backing the round were Ballistic Ventures, Canon Capital, Greenfield Partners Ltd., Lightspeed Management Co., Red Dot Capital Partners LP and TLV Partners, along with investor Eyal Waldman. Waldman co-founded Mellanox Technologies Ltd., which Nvidia Corp. bought for $6.9 billion.

Oligo first surfaced publicly in February 2023 with $28 million from Lightspeed, Ballistic and TLV. The company puts its funding to date at $140 million.

Mic McCully, field chief technology officer of Oligo, spoke with theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio, in June, where he discussed how the company delivers runtime protection in the new age of AI-driven attacks.

# A message from John Furrier, co-founder of SiliconANGLE: [...] “AI has fundamentally changed the economics of exploitation,” said Nadav Czerninski, co-founder and chief executive of Oligo. “When attackers can find vulnerabilities and build exploits at machine speed, runtime becomes the only place you can definitively understand true risk and stop real attacks without breaking production.”

Oligo put annual recurring revenue growth at 300% for the past year. Valuation has more than doubled since Greenfield Partners Ltd. led a $50 million Series B in January 2025, though the company gave no dollar figure for either.
